text:
maria: Heads-up — ran a sim overnight on tenant colocation rules + compaction. Results look promising but there are tradeoffs, so wanted input before a canary.

simon: can you paste the numbers? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: baseline fragmentation = 0.23 (23%), avg spare GPUs per rack = 0.6, tail latency delta +3–5% at p95 for small-chat workloads due to KV cache misses. With slot-aware packing + soft-affinity frag -> 0.09, overall GPU-hours saved ~14% but preemptions increase ~1.2%.

lee: what exactly is slot-aware in your sim? short version pls.

maria: slot-aware = treat GPUs as slabs (4/8/16) and prefer packing same-tenant jobs into a slab to improve batching locality and KV cache reuse. Soft-affinity allows cross-tenant fills only when global utilization < threshold (we tried 55%). Anti-affinity still enforced for tenants that opt-out.

eli: did you account for migration costs? moving checkpoints/KV is expensive and can negate gains.

maria: yes — we charged 0.8 GPU-hours per compaction move (includes checkpoint transfer + re-scheduling time). We also simulated network spikes: worst-case 100GB KV transfer per move added ~20ms p95 to co-located apps, so compaction window restricted.

catie: what's the suggested rollout and guardrails?

maria: propose a phased rollout:
1) Canary in us-west1 on a dedicated pool (20% of capacity) for 2 weeks.
2) Start with fill_threshold=0.55 and slab_sizes [4,8].
3) Enable compaction only in maintenance window 01:00–05:00 UTC, cap moves to 50/hr.
4) Gates: fragmentation_ratio < 12%, preemptions/hr < 2%, no network packet-drop spikes >2%.

lee: can you share the scheduler snippet you tested?

maria: ```
# scheduler config (sim)
packing:
  mode: slot-aware
  slab_sizes: [4,8]
  soft_affinity: true
  fill_threshold: 0.55
compaction:
  window: "01:00-05:00"
  max_moves_per_hour: 50
  migrate_cost_gpu_hours: 0.8
``` 

simon: please add metric hooks: fragmentation_ratio, preemptions_per_hour, avg_kv_move_gb, rack_net_spike_count, and 95th latency for small-chat and embeddings.

maria: will add. dashboard + synthetic job suite to validate.

sre-oncall: noted. We'll schedule extra monitoring during compaction windows. If packet drops >2% or rack CPU >85% we'll abort compaction automatically.

devops-bot: deploy started to canary pool (build 2026.3.11-762). :satellite:

maria: thanks — I'll open a short RFC with sim data, config diff, and the dashboard links. tagging @sre-oncall and @catie for rollout signoff.

simon: thanks, LGTM to test in canary as long as we keep the conservative thresholds.

eli: keep an eye on cross-region balancing too — if us-west1 packs too well we might need to route some spill to us-east.

maria: good point — will add a routing guard to avoid creating region hotspots. follow-ups in the RFC.
